Theme

Work & responsibility

labour noun and verb

hard work, toil

also labor, toil, manual labour, physical work, to labour, toil away, hard work

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.35: Labor est fūnctiō quaedam vel animī vel corporis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 398, 408

labor, labōris m.

noun, third declension

labour, toil, exertion

Work that costs effort and tires, of body or mind; Cicero sets it apart from pain, dolor (Tusc. 2.35). It also means hardship and trouble, and the result of toil (Lewis & Short). For effort in the sense of pains taken, see effort (opera). An old nominative labōs is in Plautus, Terence and Sallust.

Other words

  • labōrō, labōrāre, labōrāvī, labōrātum — to labour, toil, work hard

    verb, first conjugation, intransitive · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.121: sēsē sibi labōrāre (Lewis & Short)

    Also to take pains over something (labōrāre ut), and to be in difficulty or suffer: ex pedibus labōrāre, to have trouble with one’s feet (Lewis & Short).

  • opera, operae f. — work given or sold; manual labour

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.150: quōrum operae, nōn quōrum artēs emuntur (Lewis & Short)

    Work as a service rendered, especially the hired hand’s labour as against a skill; in the plural also the labourers themselves, “hands” (Lewis & Short). Its everyday sense is effort, pains (see effort).

  • opus arduum — hard work, a hard task

    also used · classical · Traupman 325

Examples

  • Labor est fūnctiō quaedam vel animī vel corporis, gravioris operis et mūneris.

    Labour is a kind of exertion of mind or body in some heavier task or duty.Cic. Tusc. 2.35 (Lewis & Short)

  • ut ingenium est omnium hominum ā labōre prōclīve ad libīdinem

    as every man’s nature slides away from work towards pleasureTer. And. 1.1.51 (Lewis & Short)

  • illīberālēs et sordidī quaestūs mercēnāriōrum omnium, quōrum operae, nōn quōrum artēs emuntur

    ungentlemanly and mean are the earnings of all hired workers, whose labour is bought, not their skillCic. Off. 1.150 (Lewis & Short)

  • canta, sed ambulā: labōrem cōnsōlāre cantandō

    sing, but keep walking: comfort your toil with singingAug. Serm. 256.3

See also effort, workman, employee, job, be in labour.
